text:
marta: quick follow-up to the RFC — we're still seeing dashboard p95 spikes when a tenant has a lot of access rules. thinking out loud: move most RBAC checks out of the planner stage into a small query-sidecar that returns a filtered projection and a decision token. should reduce planning latency.
sam: can you paste the recent numbers? curious magnitude.
marta: current p50=45ms p95=215ms for large dashboards (100+ widgets) under load. auth evals add ~60-80ms at p95 in our traces. overall SLO target is p95 < 150ms.
anil: moving checks out could help but we need to be careful about semantics. planner currently uses row-level predicates to prune data early. sidecar would need to support equivalent predicate pushdown or we'd increase data scanned.
kevin: +1 on semantics. idea: keep lightweight predicate pushdown in planner, but move tenant-specific permission resolution to sidecar cache. sidecar returns {projection, decision_token}. planner uses token to avoid re-eval.
julie: cache invalidation is the tricky bit. permission changes must be visible quickly for admin UX. what's acceptable TTL? we can't do minutes for enterprise security.
marta: proposal: per-tenant token TTL=10s default, with immediate invalidation on explicit ACL change via control plane event. we already emit ACL-change events to metrics pipeline.
emily: how do we ensure no cross-tenant leakage? sidecar must isolate caches by tenant id and never serve cached decisions for one tenant to another. encryption at rest and per-tenant namespaces.
sam: agree. also want to see a small perf model: extra network hop to sidecar vs saved CPU in planner. most requests are intra-node — sidecar would be colocated as an in-process or local unix-socket daemon?
anil: prefer unix-socket daemon to avoid TCP overhead + simpler auth. example config sketch:

```
# sidecar.conf
listen: unix:///var/run/console-sidecar.sock
cache_size: 10000
ttl_default_s: 10
invalidate_topic: projects/acl/changes
```

kevin: looks good. operationally we need metrics: sidecar.cache_hits, sidecar.latency_ms(p50/p95), planner.auth_eval_time. add a canary dashboard.

infra-bot: deploy-plan created: canary=5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%. rollback threshold: auth-error-rate > 0.05% or p95 increase > 10%.

julie: security review: need a threat note for token poisoning and replay. decision tokens should be HMACed with per-tenant key and short lived.

sec-team: agreed. store keys in KMS and rotate monthly. require sidecar to verify token signature before using it to skip checks.

emily: corner-case: long-running queries with pagination — token must include snapshot version or manifest to remain valid for the query lifetime. otherwise page 2 could see different results.

anil: suggestion: token contains request-id + timestamp + tenant-version. sidecar verifies tenant-version against control plane; if mismatch, planner falls back to full eval.

marta: OK plan summary: implement sidecar (unix-socket) with per-tenant cache, HMAC tokens, immediate invalidation on ACL-change events, default TTL 10s, canary 5% -> metrics + rollback rules. will put RFC follow-up doc in GH and PR a small prototype.

sam: can you add a tiny smoke test? curl example:

```
curl --unix-socket /var/run/console-sidecar.sock \
  -H "X-Tenant: t-123" \
  --data '{"query":"resolve-perms","user":"u-55","resources":["d:42"]}'
```

marta: yea i'll add tests and a dashboard. tagging @kevin @julie to pair on infra + sec validation. :thumbsup:

kevin: i'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to walk the rollout steps.

emily: small nit — add metric for decision_token_miss -> we need to see how often planner falls back.

marta: noted. thanks everyone. I'll publish the follow-up doc and link the PR to this thread."
